change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut
findings.body: The matcher reads the grant from the wrong position and inverts the check. The encoded id is session(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2) + ':' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:79-81, 114-117), so the grant is at chars 4-5. Line 483 reads substring(3, 5), which is the second token-type char plus the first grant char. It also returns false when that slice EQUALS the expected grant, which is the opposite of what a match needs. Net effect: any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` passes. expectCodeToToken (line 145) would accept `onrtro:<uuid>` for a password-grant token. The four call sites (145, 173, 182, 244) therefore do not check the grant their names promise. Fix: `items[0].length() == 6 && items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` must hold, otherwise return false. The comment on line 482 ('starts at character 4th char') is also off by one.

findings.title: client_credentials tokens are encoded with 'na', not the registered 'cc'
findings.body: The 'cc' shortcut is registered here, but the grant never records it. ClientCredentialsGrantType.java:140-141 builds the token with responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never calls clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...). Compare OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 and ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, which do. initToken (TokenManager.java:1053) then gets a null attribute and encodes UNKNOWN 'na' (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57-60). Service-account access tokens therefore carry a '...na:<uuid>' id, with no error and no test covering it. Fix: set the attribute (OAuth2Constants.CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, or context.getGrantType()) before line 140 in ClientCredentialsGrantType.java.

findings.title: UMA permission tokens are encoded with 'na', not the registered 'pg'
findings.body: 'pg' is registered here, but the UMA path never records it. PermissionGrantType.java:187 calls AuthorizationTokenService.authorize, which builds the RPT at AuthorizationTokenService.java:357-358 with responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute. The RPT id is therefore encoded as 'na'. Fix: set the attribute to OAuth2Constants.UMA_GRANT_TYPE before line 357 in AuthorizationTokenService.java. Confidence is medium because I read the call chain, not every branch of authorize().

findings.title: Non-standard token exchange tokens are encoded with 'na'
findings.body: Only StandardTokenExchangeProvider sets the grant attribute (StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237). The V1, subject-impersonation and federated providers extend AbstractTokenExchangeProvider, and their token is built at AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:409-410 with no attribute, so their ids carry 'na' although 'te' is registered for this grant. Fix: set OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE before line 409, if that method is reached by those providers and not overridden by StandardTokenExchangeProvider. I did not confirm each provider's call path.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason
findings.body: The test catches RuntimeException, so any runtime failure passes. In this test, the factory's sessionFactory is never set (it is set only in postInit, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:66, and the test never calls postInit). For 'ac' the grant lookup misses (not in the test map), and getGrantTypeByShortcut then dereferences the null sessionFactory (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:121-125), throwing an NPE that the catch swallows. The intended failure is IllegalArgumentException from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:93. Fix: expect IllegalArgumentException specifically (for example @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class)), or assert on the message.

findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked; the grantType check is duplicated
findings.body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) with the rawTokenId message, so rawTokenId is not checked at all and a null id is accepted and encoded as '...:null'. Current callers never pass null (initToken passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), and the decoder passes a substring). Fix: requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...) on that line.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcuts; the format requires 2 letters
findings.body: Every shortcut is 2 characters (ac, cc, ...), and the decoder requires exactly 6 characters for session + token type + grant (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81). postInit checks only uniqueness (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:81-86), so a 3-letter shortcut encodes fine but cannot be decoded. Fix: correct the Javadoc to 2 characters, and validate the length in postInit.

findings.title: New abstract method on an SPI interface breaks out-of-tree grant factories
findings.body: Adding getShortcut() without a default breaks every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation not in this repo. postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:72-74) calls getShortcut() on every registered grant factory, so an implementation compiled against the old interface fails at startup with AbstractMethodError. server-spi-private is an internal SPI, so this may be acceptable. If it is not, give the method a default that returns null and skip null shortcuts when building the maps.

findings.title: Token creation now dereferences the session's client context unconditionally
findings.body: getShouldUseLightweightToken calls session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) with no null check (line 86). Before this PR it ran only inside mapper transforms. Now initToken calls it for every access token (TokenManager.java:1052-1054, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54). Callers that create access tokens without a session context client would throw an NPE: PolicyEvaluationService.java:289, ClientScopeEvaluateResource.java:223-224 and 254-255, and KeycloakIdentity.java:148. None of those files calls getContext().setClient. Question: is the context client set in those admin or REST paths? If not, a client with no lightweight-aware mapper now fails where it used to succeed. Fix would be a null check that defaults to the regular token.

findings.title: PR body says 'shorter' token encoding, but the access token id gets longer
findings.body: The PR body says 'Shorter encoding of access token'. In this part the access token id changes from a 36-character UUID to '<6 chars>:<36 chars>', i.e. 43 characters (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117). Question: is the 'shorter' claim about something other than the jti? If so, the PR description should say what it means.

findings.title: Unused import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
findings.body: The import added on line 50 is never used. The only other reference to this file is OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE on line 237. Remove the import.

contracts.action: Access token id is produced by the encoder on every token issuance (initToken)
contracts.before_after: Before: the id is a bare UUID. After: the id is '<session 2><tokenType 2><grant 2>:<uuid>', built from clientSessionCtx. The encoder reads the tokenType from getShouldUseLightweightToken, which reads session.getContext().getClient() unconditionally.
contracts.visible_effect: The jti claim and the TOKEN_ID event detail change format. AssertEvents now expects the new format for code, device, refresh and CIBA events.
contracts.failure_mode: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for an unknown session type, token type or grant, so issuance fails with a 500. getShouldUseLightweightToken throws an NPE when the session has no context client (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:86). Both are visible, not silent. I found no registered grant that reaches the unknown-grant throw.
contracts.open_question: Does the admin and REST path (PolicyEvaluationService, ClientScopeEvaluateResource, KeycloakIdentity) ever run with session.getContext().getClient() null? I did not find a setClient call on those paths.

contracts.action: Grant type is recorded for the code, CIBA, device and ROPC grants via createTokenResponse
contracts.before_after: Before: no grant attribute. After: the attribute is set to context.getGrantType() (the raw grant_type form value) before createClientAccessToken. ROPC sets it right after attachSession and before responseBuilder.
contracts.visible_effect: Code, device and CIBA token ids carry the grant shortcut ac, dg and ci. ROPC carries ro.
contracts.failure_mode: If context.getGrantType() were null the attribute would be null and the id would silently encode 'na'. TokenEndpoint dispatches by grant id, so the value is always a registered id here.

contracts.action: Client credentials grant issues a service-account token
contracts.before_after: Before: a bare UUID id. After: no attribute is set, so initToken encodes 'na'. The registered 'cc' shortcut is never used by this path.
contracts.visible_effect: Service-account access tokens get an id ending in 'na:' instead of 'cc:'. The grant context is lost and no test checks it.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. Nothing fails. The encoded grant is wrong for every client_credentials token.

contracts.action: Refresh token grant re-issues the access token
contracts.before_after: Before: no attribute. After: the attribute is set to REFRESH_TOKEN ('rt') before the token is recreated, and that attribute is on the same clientSessionCtx that initToken reads.
contracts.visible_effect: Refreshed access tokens carry the 'rt' grant shortcut, and AssertEvents.expectRefresh checks it.
contracts.failure_mode: If the attribute were set after createClientAccessToken, the token would silently encode 'na'. Here it is set first, so there is no problem.

contracts.action: Pre-authorized code grant issues a token
contracts.before_after: Before: no attribute. After: the attribute is set on sessionContext (line 82) before createClientAccessToken (line 87), using the same object. The client on the session context is set after the attribute, which does not matter to the encoder.

contracts.action: Standard token exchange issues a token
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:407-410 (the V1, subject and federated providers, which do not set the attribute)
contracts.before_after: Before: no attribute. After: the attribute is set to TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE after validateConsents and before responseBuilder.generateAccessToken, so the standard path encodes 'te'.
contracts.visible_effect: Standard token exchange ids carry 'te'. The other providers' ids carry 'na', which is the gap reported in TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory.java:42.

contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:107-110 (the sibling pattern that sets the attribute)
contracts.before_after: Before: no attribute. After: still no attribute, so the RPT encodes 'na' although 'pg' is registered.
contracts.visible_effect: RPT ids carry 'na'. No test checks it.

contracts.action: Context copy constructor removed and grantType read from form params
contracts.before_after: Before: Context(Context) copied the fields. After: the copy constructor is gone, and the 7-arg constructor reads grantType from formParams.getFirst(grant_type).
contracts.failure_mode: formParams is non-null at the only construction site (TokenEndpoint.java:149-150). The copy constructor has no callers in the repo (grep), so removal does not break compilation here. An out-of-tree caller would not compile.

contracts.action: AssertEvents matchers for TOKEN_ID on code, device, refresh and CIBA events
contracts.equivalent_path: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:462-474 (isUUID, which is still used for REFRESH_TOKEN_ID)
contracts.before_after: Before: isUUID for TOKEN_ID. After: isAccessTokenId(grant), which should check the 6-char prefix and the uuid.
contracts.visible_effect: Tests that should fail on a wrong grant pass.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent in the tests: the matcher never checks the grant (line 483 reads the wrong slice and inverts the check).

summary: No blocker. Five findings are "fix" and the rest are "consider" or "question". Three are real encoding gaps: client_credentials ('cc'), UMA ('pg') and the non-standard token-exchange providers ('te') never record their grant type, so their token ids carry 'na'. The AssertEvents matcher does not check the grant at all, because it reads the wrong slice and inverts the check. testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE from an unset sessionFactory. Other items: a duplicated requireNonNull that never checks rawTokenId, a Javadoc that says 3 letters where the format needs 2, an unused import, a new abstract SPI method, a possible NPE in the token path with no session client, and a PR-body claim that the id gets shorter when it gets longer. Scope note: the large files (TokenManager, AssertEvents, StandardTokenExchangeProvider) were read at the changed hunks and the lines the findings depend on, not end to end. Several grant-path findings cite files outside this part as evidence, and their fixes are in those files.
